entry.title: [tinymce/tinymce] TinyMCE Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability using media plugin `data-mce-object` serialization
entry.content:
Impact

Stored XSS vulnerability in the media plugin. Attackers can inject malicious scripts via elements crafted through the data-mce-object attribute, which are created and executed before sanitization. Impacts users of TinyMCE with the media plugin enabled.

Patches

This vulnerability has been patched in TinyMCE 8.9.3 and TinyMCE 7.9.4 by ensuring that, when using the media plugin, any content created through the data-mce-object attribute is properly sanitized first.

Workarounds

No official workaround available.

Fix

To avoid this vulnerability:

Upgrade to TinyMCE 8.9.3 or higher. Upgrade to TinyMCE 7.9.4 or higher.

Acknowledgements

Tiny thanks Fariskhi Vidyan and David Vieira Kurz (HiSolutions AG) for their help identifying this vulnerability.

References

entry.title: [symfony/yaml] Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process
entry.content:
Description

Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure() recursed through lexInlineMapping() and lexInlineSequence() for every { and [ of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with maxNestingLevel. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as [[[[...]]]], exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.

Any code parsing untrusted YAML is affected. That includes #[MapRequestPayload] when the Yaml component is installed and the endpoint does not restrict acceptFormat: a single unauthenticated request with a YAML content type is enough.

Resolution

The inline lexer now enters and leaves the same nesting level as the rest of the parser, so nested inline collections are bounded by maxNestingLevel, and the parser raises a ParseException beyond it.

The patches for this issue are available here for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

Credits

We would like to thank Nicolas Grekas for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

entry.title: [symfony/symfony] Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header
entry.content:
Description

HeaderUtils::split() parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a (?<!\s) lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. HeaderBag calls it for the Cache-Control header whenever a Request is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.

A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, preg_match_all() gives up at pcre.backtrack_limit and split() returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.

Resolution

entry.title: [phpoffice/phpspreadsheet] PhpSpreadsheet: SSRF whitelist bypass via unre-validated HTTP redirect in Drawing::setPath external image loading
entry.content:
Summary

PhpSpreadsheet's Worksheet\Drawing::setPath() validates an external-image URL against an operator-supplied isWhitelisted callback once, on the initial URL only, then fetches it with file_get_contents() using a stream context that does not set follow_location => 0. A whitelisted host that returns an HTTP 302 Location: redirect to an internal target is therefore followed by PHP's HTTP wrapper (default follow_location=1, max_redirects=20) with no re-validation of the redirect hop — defeating the whitelist and yielding a blind SSRF from the server.

This is an unfixed variant of CVE-2026-59931 (GHSA-6hq5-7373-42rg, the WEBSERVICE redirect-whitelist-bypass): the follow_location => 0 fix (commit 7ef7b25e) was applied ONLY to Calculation/Web/Service.php; Worksheet/Drawing.php was never touched.

Root Cause

src/PhpSpreadsheet/Worksheet/Drawing.php:

  • Scheme allowlist at :125 (/^(http|https|file|ftp|s3):/) permits http/https (the redirect-following schemes) and runs on the initial URL only.
  • Opt-in gate if (!$allowExternal) at :128 (requires setAllowExternalImages(true); default false, BaseReader.php:55).
  • Whitelist check if ($isWhitelisted !== null && !$isWhitelisted($path)) at :131 — validates the INITIAL URL only; never re-applied after a redirect.
  • Stream context built at :140-152 sets user_agent + header (+ ssl.crypto_method for https) but omits follow_location. git grep follow_location on tag 5.9.0 yields a single hit — Service.php:45 (the CVE-2026-59931 fix) — confirming it was never added to Drawing.php.
  • Sink file_get_contents($path, false, $ctx) at :154.

Impact

Blind SSRF from the server: reach and trigger internal GET-driven endpoints, coarse internal reachability/port probing, and reach cloud-metadata endpoints. The fetched body is written to a temp file, checked with isImage() (mime image/*, or application/octet-stream with bin/emf extension), only image dimensions are stored, and the temp file is unlinked — so the response body is not exfiltrated (non-image responses fail isImage()). This is a blind GET primitive, not full response read.

Proof of Concept

  1. Attacker server https://trusted-whitelisted.example/redir.png returns 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/.
  2. evil.xlsx with xl/drawings/_rels/drawing1.xml.rels: <Relationship ... Type=".../image" Target="https://trusted-whitelisted.example/redir.png" TargetMode="External"/>.
  3. entry.title: [phpoffice/phpspreadsheet] PhpSpreadsheet: SSRF whitelist bypass via unre-validated HTTP redirect in Drawing::setPath external image loading
entry.content:
Summary

PhpSpreadsheet's Worksheet\Drawing::setPath() validates an external-image URL against an operator-supplied isWhitelisted callback once, on the initial URL only, then fetches it with file_get_contents() using a stream context that does not set follow_location => 0. A whitelisted host that returns an HTTP 302 Location: redirect to an internal target is therefore followed by PHP's HTTP wrapper (default follow_location=1, max_redirects=20) with no re-validation of the redirect hop — defeating the whitelist and yielding a blind SSRF from the server.

This is an unfixed variant of CVE-2026-59931 (GHSA-6hq5-7373-42rg, the WEBSERVICE redirect-whitelist-bypass): the follow_location => 0 fix (commit 7ef7b25e) was applied ONLY to Calculation/Web/Service.php; Worksheet/Drawing.php was never touched.

Root Cause

src/PhpSpreadsheet/Worksheet/Drawing.php:

  • Scheme allowlist at :125 (/^(http|https|file|ftp|s3):/) permits http/https (the redirect-following schemes) and runs on the initial URL only.
  • Opt-in gate if (!$allowExternal) at :128 (requires setAllowExternalImages(true); default false, BaseReader.php:55).
  • Whitelist check if ($isWhitelisted !== null && !$isWhitelisted($path)) at :131 — validates the INITIAL URL only; never re-applied after a redirect.
  • Stream context built at :140-152 sets user_agent + header (+ ssl.crypto_method for https) but omits follow_location. git grep follow_location on tag 5.9.0 yields a single hit — Service.php:45 (the CVE-2026-59931 fix) — confirming it was never added to Drawing.php.
  • Sink file_get_contents($path, false, $ctx) at :154.

Impact

Blind SSRF from the server: reach and trigger internal GET-driven endpoints, coarse internal reachability/port probing, and reach cloud-metadata endpoints. The fetched body is written to a temp file, checked with isImage() (mime image/*, or application/octet-stream with bin/emf extension), only image dimensions are stored, and the temp file is unlinked — so the response body is not exfiltrated (non-image responses fail isImage()).
